close_reason: Closed in single doc pass commit. The new '# Contract guarantees' (or '# Features') section in pkix-truststore/src/lib.rs covers this finding.
description:
pkix-truststore/src/lib.rs:314-385 documents return values as Vec<TrustAnchor>
but nowhere states whether the order of the returned vec corresponds to the
order of certs in the input.

Implementation-derived behavior (lib.rs:334, 379):

  Ok(certs.into_iter().map(TrustAnchor::from_cert).collect())

and

  for (i, bytes) in iter.into_iter().enumerate() {
      ...
      anchors.push(TrustAnchor::from_cert(cert));
  }

Both preserve input order. But neither rustdoc says so. Without a documented
contract, the maintainer is free to reorder internally — and a caller cannot
catch this with the type system.

What goes wrong for a caller in production:

  - A trust-store loader that uses 'first-match-wins' priority (anchor #0
    in the file takes precedence over anchor #5 for the same Subject DN)
    is silently broken if order is not preserved. This is a real pattern
    in PKI deployments where local roots are listed first to shadow public
    roots in dev/test environments.
  - A diagnostic tool that reports 'anchor #42 has expired' assumes the
    Vec index aligns with the PEM block index in the source file. Without
    a contract, this is not guaranteed.
  - Cross-deployment comparison ('this prod box loaded these anchors in
    this order, this dev box loaded them in a different order — why are
    we trusting different things?') becomes impossible to reason about
    if order is not in the contract.

This is a small docstring addition with no impl change. The maintainer is
already doing the right thing; it just needs to be a documented promise so
callers can depend on it and so a future refactor that breaks order is
caught at API-review time, not at deployment.

Fix: add to from_pem and from_der_iter rustdoc:

  /// The returned `Vec` preserves the order of certificates in the input
  /// (PEM block order for `from_pem`, iterator yield order for
  /// `from_der_iter`).

Same line on from_pem_file / from_der_iter file wrappers (delegate to
the underlying parser's order).
title: from_pem / from_der_iter: returned-Vec iteration order vs input order is unspecified
